companions.name: OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114 B
companions.description: The secondary star of the eclipsing binary OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114, 3.205 solar masses and 18.79 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 214.366 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius (solar radii) 18.79 +/- 0.37, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

mass.source: Secondary mass (solar masses) 3.205 +/- 0.025, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

temperature.source: Secondary log Teff 3.734 +/- 0.009, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G): 5420 K

orbit.source: OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114: P 214.3655 d and primary-eclipse time HJD 2451141.1 (arXiv:1805.04952, Table 1 (tbl:1), column $T_0$ (HJD-2450000) and table comment); i 88.7 degrees (arXiv:1805.04952, Table 6, column $i$ (deg)); e 0.036, omega 97.3 degrees (arXiv:1805.04952, Table 6, column $\omega$ (deg)); used as published: fitting the paper's radial velocities with it leaves 0.27 km/s rms against 1.89 km/s for omega + 180. HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary eclipse the secondary is in front, the component these papers call primary being the one eclipsed at phase 0. Separation from Kepler's third law with DEBCat's masses

text.card: The secondary star of OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114, a pair that eclipse each other every 214.366 days.
text.introduction: It has 3.205 solar masses and 18.79 solar radii; its partner has 3.304 and 26.33, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114: Mass, Radius and Period, from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)
